nodes.name: Ni foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: A piece of nickel foam (NF) (2×3 cm²) was cleaned by sonicating in 0.1 M HCl solution, deionized water, and ethanol for 10 min, respectively.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Ni(OH)2 Nanosheets: First, a piece of nickel foam (NF) (2×3 cm²) was cleaned by sonicating in 0.1 M HCl solution, deionized water, and ethanol for 10 min, respectively.

nodes.name: Ni(OH)2 hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 1.3 g nickel (II) nitrate hexahydrate (Ni(NO3)2·6H2O) and 1.3 g hexamethylenetetramine were dissolved in 25 mL deionized water and stirred for 30 min. Then, the NF was immersed in the above solution and transferred to a Teflon-lined autoclave, which was heated to 140°C for 4 h. After cooling to room temperature, the obtained Ni(OH)2 nanosheets supported on NF were washed with deionized water and then dried naturally.

nodes.name: Ni(OH)2 CV activation
nodes.procedure: Ni(OH)2 was treated by applying cyclic voltammetry (CV) in 1 M KOH medium at 100 mV s⁻¹ from 0 to 0.8 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) for 50 cycles without iR compensation.

nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Figure 2f, the ICP-OES results indicate that the content of Ni in the electrolyte obviously increases in the order of Ni(OH)₂ - PO₄³⁻ Ni(OH)₂ - NO₃⁻ Ni(OH)₂ Ni(OH)₂ - SO₄²⁻ and Ni(OH)₂ - SeO₄²⁻.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS shows P 2p peak at 133 eV (P-O species), N 1s at 399 eV (N-O), S 2p at 169 eV (S-O), Se 3d at 60 eV (Se-O) confirming oxyanion incorporation; Ni 2p3/2 at 856.1 eV and 2p1/2 at 854.9 eV for Ni(OH)₂ with Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ ratios of 0.66, 0.64, 0.45, 0.39, 0.4 for Ni(OH)₂-PO₄³⁻, -NO₃⁻, pure, -SO₄²⁻, -SeO₄²⁻ respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3c, the peak at around 133 eV can be ascribed to P-O species in P 2p XPS spectrum... the high-resolution XPS spectrum of Ni 2p in Ni(OH)₂ exhibits two peaks located at 856.1 and 854.9 eV...

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS at Ni K-edge shows Ni-O bond at 1.6 Å and Ni-Ni at 2.7 Å; Ni-O bond length of Ni(OH)₂-SeO₄²⁻ is 0.03 Å longer than Ni(OH)₂-PO₄³⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the Fourier transform (FT) of extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra at Ni K-edge suggests that the main peak at 1.6 Å is attributed to the Ni-O bond...

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR spectrum of Ni(OH)₂-SeO₄²⁻ shows stronger signal than Ni(OH)₂ at g = 2.24 indicating more Ni vacancies; Ni(OH)₂-PO₄³⁻ shows weaker signal.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectrum of Ni(OH)₂ - SeO₄²⁻ shows a stronger signal than that of Ni(OH)₂ at g = 2.24...

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows Co leaching amounts of 0.18, 0.21, 0.56 μg mL⁻¹ for Co(OH)₂-PO₄³⁻, Co(OH)₂, Co(OH)₂-SeO₄²⁻ respectively during CV activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure S18 (Supporting Information), the ICP-OES results reveal that the amount of Co leaching from the Co(OH)₂, Co(OH)₂ - PO₄³⁻ and Co(OH)₂ - SeO₄²⁻ is 0.21, 0.18, and 0.56 μg mL⁻¹...

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES of electrolyte shows PO₄³⁻ enhances structural stability of Fe(OH)₃ inhibiting Fe leaching while SeO₄²⁻ accelerates leaching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ICP results of the electrolyte show that PO₄³⁻ enhances the structural stability of the catalyst and inhibits the Fe leaching, while SeO₄²⁻ weakens the structural stability and accelerates the leaching (Figure S21, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of corresponding oxyanions (N-O, P-O, S-O, Se-O peaks) in Co(OH)₂-X catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS results reveal the surface element species of different catalysts as shown in Figure S19 (Supporting Information). This confirms the existence of the corresponding oxyanions in Co(OH)₂ - X.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows peaks attributed to N-O, P-O, S-O, and Se-O confirming corresponding oxyanion presence in Fe(OH)₃-X catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the presence of peaks attributed to N-O, P-O, S-O, and Se-O in the XPS indicates the existence of the corresponding oxyanions in the Fe(OH)₃ - X catalysts (Figure S22, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows Co(OH)₂-NO₃⁻ and Co(OH)₂-PO₄³⁻ maintain intact smooth nanosheet structure after CV activation while Co(OH)₂-SO₄²⁻ and Co(OH)₂-SeO₄²⁻ show serious structural damage.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface morphology of Co(OH)₂ - X identified by SEM shows that Co(OH)₂ - NO₃⁻ and Co(OH)₂ - PO₄³⁻ remain intact and a smooth surface nanosheet structure is seen even after the CV activation process (Figure S17, Supporting Information).
